panel_intro: One question at a time. Nothing here is submitted anywhere — nothing you enter leaves your browser.

danger.text: Right now, are you in immediate danger — in an active travel lane, or is there fire, smoke, or an injury?

unsafe_spot.text: Is the vehicle stopped somewhere unsafe — a travel lane, a highway shoulder, or a blind curve?

options.label: No, it's safely off the road

can_move_short.text: Can you move it a short, safe distance right now — for example, onto the shoulder?

options.label: Yes, I can move it safely
No, it can't be moved safely

crash.text: Was there a crash or collision?

hazard.text: Do you see smoke, fire, a strong fuel smell, or fluid leaking from the vehicle?

overheating.text: Is the engine overheating — temperature gauge in the red, or steam from the hood?

controls.text: Are the brakes or steering affected — soft or unresponsive brakes, or hard-to-control steering?

can_move.text: Can the vehicle move under its own power right now?

coverage.text: Do you have roadside assistance coverage — insurance, an auto club, or a manufacturer plan?

distance.text: Are you within a short, safe distance of home or a repair shop?

emergency.title: Call Emergency Services Now
emergency.summary: Call 911. Your safety comes first — this isn't a situation for an app or a calculator.
emergency.confidence_text: This is a clear, urgent situation. Don't wait for a tow truck first.
not_to_do: Don't stand near active traffic to inspect the vehicle.
Don't try to move the vehicle yourself if there's fire, smoke, or injury.
Don't wait to see if it "gets better" before calling.
before_help_checklist: Move away from traffic if you can do so safely.
Turn on hazard lights.
Call 911 and describe your exact location.
Stay on the line until you're told it's safe to hang up.

phone_script.intro: If you're able to speak, this covers what dispatchers need first.
lines: I need help — my vehicle is at [location description].
There is [fire / smoke / injury / a vehicle stopped in traffic].
I am [safe / not safe] right now.

emergency.next_action: Stay on the line with emergency services and follow their instructions.

emergency_unsafe_spot.title: Call Emergency Services Now
emergency_unsafe_spot.summary: Your vehicle is stuck somewhere dangerous and can't be moved safely. Call 911 to get traffic controlled around you, even without a crash or fire.
emergency_unsafe_spot.confidence_text: An unmovable vehicle in an active lane is a real hazard — this needs an immediate response, not a wait.
not_to_do: Don't stand behind or beside the vehicle in the travel lane.
Don't try to push or force it to move on your own.
Don't rely on hazard lights alone in low-visibility conditions.
before_help_checklist: Move yourself and any passengers away from traffic if possible.
Turn on hazard lights.
Call 911 and describe your exact location and lane.
Wave help toward you safely once it arrives.

lines: My vehicle is stopped in a travel lane at [location description] and can't be moved.
No one is injured, but this is a traffic hazard.
Can you send help to control traffic and arrange a tow?

emergency_unsafe_spot.next_action: Stay somewhere safe, away from traffic, until help arrives.

move_to_safety.title: Move Only to Immediate Safety
move_to_safety.summary: If you can move the vehicle a short, safe distance — like onto the shoulder — do that now, then stop and reassess.
move_to_safety.confidence_text: Moving a short distance can reduce real danger, but only if it's clearly safe to do so — if you have any doubt, treat this as an emergency instead.
not_to_do: Don't drive any further than the nearest safe spot.
Don't move it if doing so means crossing active traffic.
Don't assume the shoulder is safe on a blind curve or narrow road — use hazard lights either way.
before_help_checklist: Turn on hazard lights before and after moving.
Check mirrors and traffic before moving at all.
Once stopped safely, exit on the side away from traffic if possible.
Call for a tow or roadside help once you're safely stopped.

phone_script.intro: Read this while you're on the phone with help.
lines: Hi, I moved my vehicle to [location description] after it stalled in an unsafe spot.
It's safe to approach now.
Can you confirm ETA and whether I need a tow or roadside service?

move_to_safety.next_action: Once you're safely stopped, use this tool again from the top if anything about the situation has changed.

tow_after_crash.title: Do Not Drive — Call a Tow
tow_after_crash.summary: After any crash, get the vehicle towed rather than driving it — even if it looks driveable, there can be hidden damage.
tow_after_crash.confidence_text: Crash damage is often worse than it looks. This is a clear case for a tow, not a drive.
not_to_do: Don't drive away before exchanging information or documenting the scene.
Don't assume no visible damage means it's safe to drive.
Don't skip calling police if there's injury, disagreement, or significant damage.
before_help_checklist: Take photos of all vehicles and the scene.
Exchange insurance and contact information.
Call police if required in your area or if anyone disagrees about what happened.
Note the other driver's plate and insurance details.

phone_script.intro: Read this while you're on the phone with the tow company.
lines: Hi, I've been in an accident and need a tow from [location description].
The vehicle is [safe / not safe] to approach and cannot be driven.
Can you confirm total price, ETA, and where the vehicle will be taken?
Will there be storage charges, and when do they start?

tow_after_crash.next_action: Once the vehicle is towed, contact your insurer to start the claim.

tow_hazard.title: Do Not Drive — Call a Tow
tow_hazard.summary: Smoke, fire, a fuel smell, or a fluid leak all mean the vehicle isn't safe to drive further.
tow_hazard.confidence_text: These are textbook do-not-drive signs — there's no ambiguity here.
not_to_do: Don't keep driving to "just get it home."
Don't open the hood if you see active smoke or fire — call 911 instead.
Don't ignore a fuel smell, even a faint one.
before_help_checklist: Move away from the vehicle if you smell fuel or see smoke.
Turn off the engine if it's safe to do so.
Note what you saw or smelled to describe to the tow operator.
Keep bystanders and any flame source away from the vehicle.

phone_script.intro: Read this while you're on the phone with the tow company.
lines: Hi, I have a vehicle at [location description] with smoke, a fuel smell, or a fluid leak.
It is not safe to drive.
Can you confirm total price, ETA, and where it will be taken?
Are there any after-hours fees right now?

tow_hazard.next_action: Once towed, ask a mechanic to diagnose it before driving it again.

tow_overheat.title: Do Not Drive — Call a Tow
tow_overheat.summary: Driving on an overheated engine risks turning a repair into a much more expensive one.
tow_overheat.confidence_text: Overheating is a clear signal to stop driving, not a symptom to push through.
not_to_do: Don't keep driving "just a little further."
Don't open a hot radiator cap.
Don't pour cold water on a hot engine.
before_help_checklist: Turn off the engine once safely stopped.
Leave the hood closed until it's cooled — don't inspect it hot.
Note when the temperature gauge started climbing.
Avoid restarting the engine to "check" if it's fine.

phone_script.intro: Read this while you're on the phone with the tow company.
lines: Hi, my vehicle overheated and is at [location description].
It is safe to approach but should not be driven.
Can you confirm total price, ETA, and where it will be taken?
Will there be storage charges?

tow_overheat.next_action: Have a mechanic check the cooling system before driving it again.

tow_controls.title: Do Not Drive — Call a Tow
tow_controls.summary: Brakes or steering that feel off are safety-critical — this is never worth risking a drive.
tow_controls.confidence_text: Brake and steering issues are unambiguous do-not-drive signs.
not_to_do: Don't test the brakes or steering by driving further to "see how bad it is."
Don't rely on the parking brake as a substitute for working brakes.
Don't assume it's minor just because the car still moves.
before_help_checklist: Keep the vehicle stopped and stable if possible.
Use hazard lights and, if available, warning triangles.
Note exactly what felt wrong to describe to the tow operator.
Avoid restarting or moving the vehicle further.

phone_script.intro: Read this while you're on the phone with the tow company.
lines: Hi, my vehicle's brakes or steering feel unsafe. It's at [location description].
It should not be driven.
Can you confirm total price, ETA, and where it will be taken?
Are there any after-hours fees right now?

tow_controls.next_action: Have a mechanic inspect the brakes or steering before driving it again.

tow_immobile.title: Do Not Drive — Call a Tow
tow_immobile.summary: If the vehicle can't move under its own power, a tow is the straightforward next step.
tow_immobile.confidence_text: A vehicle that won't move has one clear next step — no ambiguity here.
not_to_do: Don't attempt to force-start or push it into traffic.
Don't assume a jump start alone will fix an unrelated mechanical issue.
Don't authorize a tow destination you haven't confirmed.
before_help_checklist: Turn on hazard lights.
Note any warning lights or unusual sounds beforehand.
Confirm exactly where you want the vehicle taken.
Keep your keys and paperwork accessible for the driver.

phone_script.intro: Read this while you're on the phone with the tow company.
lines: Hi, my vehicle won't move and needs a tow from [location description].
Can you confirm total price, ETA, mileage charges, and where it will be taken?
Will there be storage charges, and when do they start?

tow_immobile.next_action: Use the Tow Cost Estimator to sanity-check the price before you agree.

roadside_battery.title: Call Roadside Assistance First
roadside_battery.summary: A dead battery is one of the most common roadside calls — most plans handle a jump start quickly.
roadside_battery.confidence_text: This is a textbook roadside-assistance case.
not_to_do: Don't assume it's the battery without at least trying a jump start.
Don't keep trying to start it repeatedly — that can damage the starter.
Don't ignore repeat dead-battery issues — that can mean a bad alternator, not just the battery.
before_help_checklist: Turn off accessories (lights, AC, radio) while you wait.
Have your keys and vehicle location ready.
Note if this has happened before — it may not be just the battery.
Stay with the vehicle if it's safe to do so.

phone_script.intro: Read this while you're on the phone with roadside assistance.
lines: Hi, my vehicle won't start — I think it's the battery. I'm at [location description].
It's safe to approach and I'm waiting nearby.
Can you confirm ETA and whether a jump start is included?

roadside_battery.next_action: If the battery dies again soon after, get it tested rather than just jumped again.

roadside_tire.title: Call Roadside Assistance First
roadside_tire.summary: A flat tire is usually a quick roadside fix — a spare swap, or a tow only if there's no usable spare.
roadside_tire.confidence_text: This is a textbook roadside-assistance case.
not_to_do: Don't drive on a flat, even slowly — it can destroy the wheel.
Don't change a tire yourself on the traffic side of the vehicle.
Don't assume your spare is ready — check it's inflated before relying on it.
before_help_checklist: Pull as far off the road as safely possible.
Turn on hazard lights.
Check whether you have a usable spare and the tools for it.
Stay on the side away from traffic while you wait.

phone_script.intro: Read this while you're on the phone with roadside assistance.
lines: Hi, I have a flat tire at [location description].
It's safe to approach.
Can you confirm ETA, and whether you can swap in my spare or if I'll need a tow?

roadside_tire.next_action: Get the flat repaired or replaced properly before driving on the spare long-term.

roadside_lockout.title: Call Roadside Assistance First
roadside_lockout.summary: Most roadside and insurance plans include lockout service — rarely worth a locksmith call-out fee on your own.
roadside_lockout.confidence_text: This is a textbook roadside-assistance case.
not_to_do: Don't try to force a door or window open yourself — that can cause real damage.
Don't leave the area if a child or pet is locked inside — call 911 first in that case.
Don't pay a locksmith before checking if your plan already covers it.
before_help_checklist: Check all doors and the trunk, just in case.
Have ID or proof of ownership ready if asked.
Note your exact location for dispatch.
Stay near the vehicle if it's safe to do so.

phone_script.intro: Read this while you're on the phone with roadside assistance.
lines: Hi, I'm locked out of my vehicle at [location description].
No one and nothing unsafe is inside.
Can you confirm ETA for lockout service?

roadside_lockout.next_action: Consider a spare key or key fob backup so this is a one-time issue.

roadside_fuel.title: Call Roadside Assistance First
roadside_fuel.summary: Running out of fuel is a simple roadside delivery in most cases.
roadside_fuel.confidence_text: This is a textbook roadside-assistance case.
not_to_do: Don't walk along a highway shoulder to find fuel yourself if it's unsafe.
Don't run the engine repeatedly trying to coax out the last fumes.
Don't forget some plans limit free fuel delivery to a small amount.
before_help_checklist: Pull as far off the road as safely possible.
Turn on hazard lights.
Confirm your plan covers fuel delivery, not just towing.
Stay with the vehicle if it's safe to do so.

phone_script.intro: Read this while you're on the phone with roadside assistance.
lines: Hi, I've run out of fuel at [location description].
It's safe to approach.
Can you confirm ETA and whether fuel delivery is included in my plan?

roadside_fuel.next_action: Keep an eye on your gauge going forward — running dry can also damage a fuel pump over time.

roadside_general.title: Call Roadside Assistance First
roadside_general.summary: Your situation isn't clear-cut, but you have coverage and no safety-critical signs — roadside assistance is the right first call.
roadside_general.confidence_text: The symptom is ambiguous, so treat this as a starting point, not a diagnosis.
not_to_do: Don't keep driving if anything changes or gets worse.
Don't assume it's minor just because it's not obvious.
Don't skip mentioning any warning lights when you call.
before_help_checklist: Note any warning lights, sounds, or smells.
Have your policy or membership number ready.
Stay somewhere safe while you wait.
Ask the dispatcher what to expect if they can't fix it roadside.

phone_script.intro: Read this while you're on the phone with roadside assistance.
lines: Hi, I'm having car trouble at [location description] and I'm not sure exactly what's wrong.
It's safe to approach and the vehicle can move.
Can you confirm ETA, and what happens if it needs a tow instead?

roadside_general.next_action: If roadside assistance can't resolve it, use the Tow Cost Estimator next.

reassess.title: Safe to Reassess
reassess.summary: Nothing here points to a safety-critical issue. If you're close to home or a shop, driving cautiously may be reasonable — but stay alert.
reassess.confidence_text: This is the least certain outcome — it depends on details this tool can't see or measure. When in doubt, treat it more cautiously than this.
not_to_do: Don't continue if anything changes — new noise, smell, warning light, or handling issue.
Don't drive further than necessary "just to see."
Don't ignore a gut feeling that something's wrong.
before_help_checklist: Plan the most direct, low-speed route to safety.
Keep your phone charged and accessible.
Pull over immediately if anything changes.
Have a roadside or tow number ready just in case.

phone_script.intro: Keep this ready in case things change on the way.
lines: Hi, I'm currently driving cautiously from [location description] toward [destination] and noticed [symptom].
I may need a tow or roadside help if anything changes.
Can you confirm ETA and pricing in case I call back?

reassess.next_action: If you're not confident, treat this as a tow situation instead — it's the safer default.

tow_general.title: Do Not Drive — Call a Tow
tow_general.summary: With an unclear symptom, no roadside coverage, and no safe destination nearby, a tow is the safer default.
tow_general.confidence_text: This isn't a clear emergency, but without coverage or a short safe drive, towing is the more reliable choice than guessing.
not_to_do: Don't drive further to "test it out" on an unclear symptom.
Don't skip asking for a total price before the truck is dispatched.
Don't agree to storage before asking if it can be avoided.
before_help_checklist: Note any warning lights, sounds, or smells to describe.
Confirm exactly where you want the vehicle taken.
Keep your keys and paperwork accessible.
Ask about total price before the truck arrives.

phone_script.intro: Read this while you're on the phone with the tow company.
lines: Hi, I'm having car trouble at [location description] and I'm not sure exactly what's wrong.
I don't have roadside coverage and I'm not near a safe destination.
Can you confirm total price, ETA, mileage charges, and where it will be taken?

tow_general.next_action: Use the Tow Cost Estimator to sanity-check the price before you agree.
